notes:
ADVERSARIAL COMPARISON, attempt 1, candidate-1.png vs /images/hem/round-hem.jpg.

WHAT THE BLUEPRINT DRAWS: an isolated hem-edge schematic centred on the side seam. The seam is drawn as a solid vertical line flanked by two dashed topstitch rows, dropping from the top of the frame and terminating in a small cusp exactly where it meets the hem. From that cusp the red hem edge falls away in BOTH directions in one continuous smooth curve - toward the front panel on one side and the back panel on the other - so the hem is at its HIGHEST at the side seam and longest at front and back. A second dashed curve runs parallel to the hem edge for its full length (the narrow topstitched hem). There is no vent slit, no squared or level segment, and no gusset panel.

WHAT THE PHOTO SHOWS: a near-profile detail of the lower shirt. A topstitched vertical side seam runs down the centre of frame and terminates in a small cusp at the hem apex. From that apex the hem descends both toward the front (frame left, to roughly y=745) and toward the back (frame right, to roughly y=820) in one continuous curve. Highest point of the hem is precisely at the side seam. A narrow rolled hem edge follows the whole curve. No vent slit at the seam, no squared segment, no gusset. Photoreal cotton poplin on a real model (visible skin/hand, not a mannequin), no line-art or CGI look.

REJECTION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED (i.e. checks the photo survived):
- Straight-hem contamination: none - the hem is continuously curved with zero level run.
- Side-vent contamination (hem-straight-side-vents / hem-sq-side-vents-5cm): none - the side seam closes cleanly into the hem apex with no slit.
- Small-round-hem contamination: no - the rise from the front low point up to the seam apex is generous, matching the blueprint's deep sweep rather than a shallow one.
- Gusset contamination: correctly absent (see below).
- Face/orientation error: spec orientation is 'detail'; the photo is a macro crop with no full-garment silhouette, centred on the same side-seam region the drawing isolates, spanning front and back exactly as drawn. No front/back swap.
- Inverted geometry (the single most likely failure for this option - hem dipping at the seam instead of rising): did NOT occur. The apex is unambiguously at the seam.
- Text / annotation / watermark / ruler / dimension callout traced from the drawing: none anywhere in frame; no red or coloured guide marks survived into the photo.
- Location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props: none; background is seamless light grey.

SIDE GUSSET - DOCUMENTED NON-ISSUE: the auto-generated part-level checklist for 'shirt-hem' lists 'side gusset' among features to reproduce, and the built prompt therefore instructed the model to render one. The BLUEPRINT DEPICTS NO GUSSET - gussets belong to the sibling options hem-round-pentagon-gusset, hem-round-hexagon-gusset, hem-large-round-triangle-gusset and hem-small-round-pentagon-gusset. Under the Supreme Rule (the drawing is law, and the prompt's own FORBIDDEN block bars geometry borrowed from a neighbouring option on the same field) the correct output is no gusset. The photo renders no gusset, so this checklist line is vacuously satisfied. Had a gusset appeared it would have been a CRITICAL sibling-contamination error; it did not.

SYMMETRY: the back tail falls slightly lower/longer than the front tail. This matches the blueprint, whose own curve descends further on one side, and matches real worn drape on a garment photographed in profile. The construction-symmetry requirement that matters for this option - the hem rises at the side seam on both the front and back side - is fully satisfied. Not scored as a defect.

DIMENSIONS / ANGLES: the extracted spec carries no dimensions, angles or counts (measured.shapes = ['curved hem'] only), so there is no numeric tolerance to violate; these categories were graded on proportional fidelity of the rise-to-run of the curve, which tracks the drawing.

CONCLUSION: a faithful, unobstructed, annotation-free reproduction of the drawn round/shirttail hem. Two minor cosmetic observations, no critical or major discrepancies.
